operations.description:
Approve a pending cancellation request for an order item.

This operation allows sellers to approve customer cancellation requests for their order items. When a seller approves a cancellation request, the system immediately changes the request status to 'approved', creates an immutable snapshot of the approval action for audit trail purposes, marks the order item as cancelled, and restores the item's stock quantity to available inventory.

The seller approval is final and cannot be reversed. Once approved, the cancellation request moves from 'pending' to 'approved' state, and the customer will receive a refund for the cancelled item. The seller can optionally provide a response message, though the approval action itself does not require additional input parameters.

This operation is restricted to the seller who owns the order item's products. Customers cannot approve their own cancellation requests - only the seller can make this decision. The system validates that the requesting seller is the correct seller for the order item before processing the approval.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
1. Validate cancellation request exists and is not deleted (check deleted_at is NULL)
2. Validate cancellation request status is 'pending' - only pending requests can be approved
3. Verify the requesting seller_id matches the cancellation_request's seller_id
4. Create a snapshot record in ecommerce_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots before any state changes
5. Update cancellation request status from 'pending' to 'approved'
6. Update the associated order_item status to 'cancelled'
7. Create an inventory record to restore stock quantity for the cancelled item
8. Log the approval action in activity_logs table for audit trail
9. Return the updated cancellation request with 'approved' status

responseBody.description: Updated cancellation request showing approved status

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the cancellation request to approve
parameters.name: cancellationRequestId

operations.description:
Reject a cancellation request submitted by a customer for one of the seller's order items.

This operation allows sellers to deny a customer's cancellation request for an order item they sold. When a seller rejects a request, the cancellation request status changes to "rejected" and the item continues processing normally with its original paid status.

The seller must be authenticated and must be the owner of the order item referenced by the cancellation request. The system validates that the seller has permission to respond to this specific request before processing the rejection.

Upon successful rejection, the cancellation request is updated with a rejected status. A snapshot record is automatically created in the audit trail table to preserve the state before rejection, the seller's rejection action, and the timestamp for dispute resolution and historical reference.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
Retrieve the cancellation request by cancellationRequestId from the database.

Validate authentication: Ensure the requesting actor is an authenticated seller.

Validate ownership: Fetch the order_item_id from the cancellation request, then verify that the seller_id of the order item matches the authenticated seller's ID. Return 403 Forbidden if not authorized.

Validate state: Check that the cancellation request status is "pending". Only pending requests can be rejected. Return 400 Bad Request if status is already "approved" or "rejected".

Update the cancellation request: Set status to "rejected", create an optional seller_response note (NULL if not provided).

Create snapshot: Insert a new record into ecommerce_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots with actor_type="seller", status_before="pending", status_after="rejected", action="rejected", and current timestamp.

Return the updated cancellation request object.

Error handling: Return 404 Not Found if the cancellation request does not exist. Return 403 Forbidden if the seller is not authorized. Return 400 Bad Request if the request is not in pending status.

responseBody.description: The updated cancellation request with rejected status

parameters.description: ID of the cancellation request to reject
parameters.name: cancellationRequestId

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of refund requests submitted by customers for delivered order items.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities for refund requests, allowing customers to view their own requests, sellers to view refund requests for their order items, and administrators to view all refund requests across the platform.

Search and filtering options include refund request status (pending, approved, rejected), date ranges for request submission and approval/rejection dates, order item references, customer identification, seller identification, refund reason keywords, and refund amounts. The endpoint supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes, cursor-based navigation for large result sets, and flexible sorting options.

Each refund request in the results includes essential information such as request ID, status, order item details, refund amount, customer reference, and timestamps for creation and status changes. For approved refunds, the operation also indicates whether stock has been restored to the product variant.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_refund_requests table with optional filters for status, date ranges, order_item_id, customer_id, and seller_id.

Apply search filters:
- status: Filter by refund request status (pending, approved, rejected)
- orderItemId: Filter by specific order item ID
- customerIds: Filter by list of customer IDs (for admin view)
- sellerIds: Filter by list of seller IDs (for admin view)
- reasonKeywords: Partial text match on customer-provided refund reason
- startDate: Filter requests created on or after this date
- endDate: Filter requests created on or before this date
- minAmount: Filter requests with refund amount >= this value
- maxAmount: Filter requests with refund amount <= this value

Join with ecommerce_mall_order_items to filter by seller ownership.
Join with ecommerce_mall_customers for customer filtering.
Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variants to verify stock restoration status for approved refunds.

Return cursor-based pagination with:
- hasNextPage: Boolean indicating more results available
- nextPageCursor: Cursor string for next page (if hasNextPage is true)
- total: Total count of matching results

operations.description:
Create a new refund request for a delivered order item.

This operation allows customers to request a refund for individual order items that have already been delivered. The system validates that the target order item has a 'delivered' status before creating the refund request, as per business rules only delivered items are eligible for refund requests.

The refund request is associated with a specific order item and the customer who places the order. Upon creation, the system automatically generates a snapshot to preserve the initial state of the refund request for audit trail and dispute resolution purposes. The refund request enters a 'Pending' state and will be processed by the seller for approval or rejection.

Additionally, the system validates that the refund request is submitted within 7 days of the item's delivery date. If the 7-day window has expired, the refund request creation will be rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new refund request in the ecommerce_mall_refund_requests table.

1. Validate order item existence and retrieve it from ecommerce_mall_order_items table using the orderItemId path parameter.
2. Verify the order item status equals 'delivered' - if not, return a 400 Bad Request error indicating the item is not eligible for refund.
3. Validate the current customer making the request is the owner of the order containing this order item.
4. Create a new refund request record with:
   - orderItemId: from path parameter
   - customerId: from authenticated session
   - status: 'submitted'
   - reason: from request body
   - createdAt: current timestamp
5. Create an audit snapshot in ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots table capturing the initial state of the refund request.
6. Create a customer-specific snapshot in ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshot_of_customers table.
7. Return the created refund request with full details.

parameters.description: The ID of the order item that the refund request is for. The order item must have a 'delivered' status to be eligible for refund.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of audit snapshots for a specific refund request, showing the complete history of state changes and seller responses.

Each snapshot represents a point-in-time record of the refund request state when changes were made, such as when a seller approved or rejected the request, when the status changed, or when the reason/response was updated. Snapshots are immutable audit trail records that provide a complete chronological history of the refund request lifecycle.

The endpoint supports advanced filtering and sorting capabilities, allowing you to narrow results by action type (created, status_changed, approved, rejected), date ranges, or specific status transitions. Results are returned with cursor-based pagination for efficient handling of large result sets.

Access control ensures customers can only view snapshots for refund requests they initiated, while administrators and super administrators have platform-wide visibility for dispute resolution and oversight purposes. All snapshot records remain preserved even if the associated refund request is deleted, maintaining the audit trail for compliance and legal requirements.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots table filtered by refund_request_id path parameter.

Apply pagination: retrieve snapshot records with cursor-based pagination using created_at as cursor field.

Apply optional filters:
- action_type filter: exact match or IN clause for action_type (created, status_changed, approved, rejected, response_added)
- date range filter: created_at BETWEEN start_date AND end_date
- status_before filter: exact match on status_before field
- status_after filter: exact match on status_after field

Apply sorting:
- Primary sort: created_at DESC (newest first, default)
- Secondary sort options: refund_request_id ASC/DESC, actor_type ASC/DESC

Execute query with JOIN to ecommerce_mall_refund_requests to validate refund_request_id exists and fetch associated refund_code for response.

Return paginated results with metadata: total count, has_next_page, next_cursor, current page size.

Authorization: customer actor can view snapshots only for their own refund requests (validate ecommerce_mall_customer_id matches current user). Admin/super_admin actors can view any refund request snapshots on the platform.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific refund request snapshot from the audit trail for dispute resolution and historical reference.

This operation returns a single snapshot record that captures the state of a refund request at a specific point in time, typically when a seller responded with approval or rejection. Snapshots preserve the complete history of the refund request workflow including status transitions, reason changes, and seller responses.

The snapshot contains comprehensive before/after value comparisons showing:
- Status transitions (pending → approved/rejected/refunded)
- Customer reason changes made during the workflow
- Seller response text and rejection reasons
- Timestamp of each change for chronological dispute resolution
- Actor accountability (which customer, seller, or admin made each change)

**Authorized actors who can view refund request snapshots:**
- The customer who initiated the refund request
- The seller who responded to the refund request  
- Platform administrators (admin and superAdmin actors) for dispute resolution and compliance auditing

Snapshots serve as the authoritative audit trail for post-delivery dispute resolution, providing complete historical reference of the entire refund request lifecycle. While snapshots capture immutable business decisions, they support soft deletion for administrative cleanup while preserving the historical record.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve a single refund request snapshot by ID from the ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots table.

1. Query the database for the snapshot matching the provided snapshotId
2. Verify ownership/authorization:
   - Customer actor: verify the snapshot's parent refund request belongs to them (ecommerce_mall_refund_requests.ecommerce_mall_customer_id = actor.id)
   - Seller actor: verify the snapshot's parent refund request's order item belongs to a product owned by this seller
   - Admin/SuperAdmin actors: always authorized
3. Return the full snapshot record including all before/after values
4. Throw 404 Not Found if snapshotId does not exist
5. Throw 403 Forbidden if the actor does not have access to this snapshot
6. Return the snapshot with all fields populated from the database schema, including:
   - id, refund_request_id, actor_type, action_type
   - status_before, status_after
   - reason_before, reason_after
   - response_before, response_after
   - metadata_before, metadata_after
   - created_at, deleted_at

The endpoint provides read-only access to immutable audit records. No modifications are allowed. Snapshots are append-only records created automatically when sellers respond to refund requests.

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of seller approval requests from the ecommerce_mall_seller_approval_requests table.

This endpoint allows administrators and super administrators to browse, filter, and search for seller registration approval requests. The operation supports filtering by request status (pending, approved, rejected), date range queries for creation or update timestamps, and optional seller-specific queries.

The response provides summary information for each approval request including the seller identifier, current status, rejection reason if applicable, and timestamps. Pagination is supported to handle large volumes of approval requests efficiently.

Administrators can use this endpoint to review pending approvals, track approved or rejected requests, and monitor the overall seller onboarding workflow. The endpoint returns summary data optimized for list views in administrative dashboards.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_seller_approval_requests table with pagination and filtering.

1. Parse request body search criteria:
   - Extract optional status filter (pending, approved, rejected)
   - Extract optional date range filters (created_after, created_before, updated_after, updated_before)
   - Extract pagination parameters (page, pageSize, cursor)
   - Extract sorting parameters (sortBy, sortOrder)

2. Build database query with WHERE clause:
   - Apply status filter if provided: status = :status
   - Apply date range filters if provided
   - Apply soft delete filter: deleted_at IS NULL

3. Execute query with:
   - Pagination limit and offset or cursor-based pagination
   - Sorting by specified field in specified order
   - Return only summary fields needed for list display

4. Execute COUNT query for total records to return pagination metadata

5. Return paginated response with:
   - data: Array of approval request summaries
   - pagination: { currentPage, pageSize, totalItems, totalPages }

6. Authorization: Admin and SuperAdmin roles only

responseBody.description: Paginated list of seller approval request summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering approval requests

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a seller approval request, including its current status, submission date, and administrative actions taken.

This operation provides visibility into the seller onboarding workflow by returning the complete state of a specific approval request. The response includes the request's current status (pending, approved, or rejected), the seller account information, and if rejected, the reason provided by the administrator.

Only the seller who submitted the request, administrators, and super administrators have access to view approval request details. This ensures that sellers can monitor their own application status while administrative reviews remain confidential from other users.

The approval request entity includes timestamps for submission and any status changes, allowing sellers to track how long their application has been under review. When a request is approved, the seller account becomes active and the seller can begin listing products. When rejected, the request includes the rejection reason and the seller may submit a new approval request.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_seller_approval_requests table using the approvalRequestId UUID parameter.

Perform a single-row SELECT with all columns including status, rejectionReason, submittedAt, and approvalTimestamp fields.

Join with ecommerce_mall_sellers table to include seller account details (sellerId, seller email, profile information) in the response.

Apply authorization checks: only allow access if the requesting actor is the seller who owns the request, or has admin/superAdmin privileges.

Return 404 Not Found if the approvalRequestId does not exist in the database.

Include all snapshot-related fields from ecommerce_mall_seller_approval_snapshots if available for audit trail purposes.

Response includes: approvalRequestId, sellerId, status (pending/approved/rejected), submission timestamp, any administrative timestamps (approvedAt/rejectedAt), rejection reason if applicable, and seller account details.

responseBody.description: Detailed seller approval request information including status, timestamps, seller details, and administrative actions

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the seller approval request to retrieve
parameters.name: approvalRequestId

operations.description:
Update the approval status of a seller's registration request.

This operation allows platform administrators to review seller approval requests and change their status from pending to either approved or rejected. Only users with administrator privileges (admin or superAdmin roles) can perform this operation.

When approving a request, the seller account becomes active and gains full selling capabilities on the platform. When rejecting a request, the seller cannot sell and must view the rejection reason to understand why their application was denied. Rejected sellers may submit a new approval request after addressing the issues noted in the rejection.

The operation creates an immutable audit snapshot before applying the status change, preserving the previous state and recording which administrator made the decision. This snapshot is essential for dispute resolution and historical tracking of the approval workflow.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update seller approval request status and optionally set rejection reason.

1. Validate approval request exists and is not soft-deleted
2. Verify current user has admin or superAdmin role
3. Accept new status value (approved or rejected)
4. If status is rejected, rejection_reason is required
5. If status is approved, rejection_reason must be null or omitted
6. Create snapshot record with from_status = current status, to_status = new status
7. Update approval request record with new status and rejection_reason
8. Return updated approval request with full details

Transaction: Snapshot creation and approval request update must be atomic.

responseBody.description: Updated seller approval request with full details

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the seller approval request to update
parameters.name: approvalRequestId

requestBody.description: Update data for approval request status and rejection reason

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of snapshot records for a specific seller approval request.

This endpoint provides access to the immutable audit trail of state changes for a seller approval request. Snapshots capture point-in-time states when the approval request was created, approved, rejected, or resubmitted. Each snapshot includes the status before and after the change, the actor who made the decision (admin or superAdmin), and timestamps for audit purposes.

Both sellers and administrators can view these snapshots for dispute resolution and audit purposes. Sellers can access snapshots for their own approval requests by providing the approval request ID, while administrators have full access to view snapshots for any approval request on the platform.

Search capabilities include filtering by status transitions (from_status, to_status), date ranges for created_at timestamps, actor types (admin, superAdmin), and rejection reasons. Results are sortable by creation timestamp or status and support cursor-based pagination for efficient large dataset browsing.

All snapshot records are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted. The system automatically excludes soft-deleted records (records with deleted_at timestamps) from results.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_seller_approval_snapshots table filtered by approvalRequestId path parameter.

Apply search filters from request body:
- Filter by from_status or to_status (pending, approved, rejected)
- Filter by actor_type (admin, superAdmin)
- Filter by created_at date range (startTime, endTime)
- Filter by presence of rejection_reason
- Filter by actor_id if provided

Apply sorting from request body:
- Sort by created_at (asc/desc)
- Sort by from_status, to_status if provided

Apply pagination:
- Page number (1-indexed) or cursor-based pagination
- Page size (1-100 records per page)

Return paginated results with total count, pagination metadata, and snapshot summary data.

Each snapshot record includes: id, from_status, to_status, actor_type, actor_id, rejection_reason, created_at timestamp.

Join with ecommerce_mall_seller_approval_requests to validate approvalRequestId exists and is not deleted.

Validate approvalRequestId matches an existing seller approval request.

Do not include deleted snapshots (soft-deleted records excluded).

Authorization: sellers can view their own approval request snapshots, admins can view all snapshots.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of seller approval request snapshot summaries

parameters.description: ID of the seller approval request whose snapshots to retrieve
parameters.name: approvalRequestId

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for snapshot listing

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific snapshot of a seller approval request for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

This operation returns detailed information about a specific point-in-time state of a seller approval request. The snapshot captures critical business events including when an approval request was approved or rejected, the reason for rejection (if applicable), and which administrator made the decision.

Snapshots are immutable audit trail records created automatically when an administrator responds to a seller approval request. They serve as authoritative records for dispute resolution and historical reference. Both the seller who submitted the approval request and platform administrators can access these snapshots.

The response includes the complete snapshot data with before and after status values, timestamps, and administrator references for accountability.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_seller_approval_snapshots table by snapshot ID.

Validate that the approvalRequestId in the path matches the snapshot's approval_request_id foreign key.

Implement access control: only the seller (ecommerce_mall_seller_id) associated with this snapshot, or any administrator (admin/superAdmin) can retrieve the snapshot.

Include polymorphic actor reference: if actor_id is populated, join with ecommerce_mall_admins or ecommerce_mall_super_admins tables to resolve actor details.

Return the snapshot with all fields: id, approvalRequestId, sellerId, actor reference, from_status, to_status, rejection_reason, and created_at.

Return 404 Not Found if snapshot does not exist.
Return 403 Forbidden if the requesting actor is not authorized (not the seller or administrator).

responseBody.description: Detailed snapshot information including status transition details and administrator decision

parameters.description: Identifier of the seller approval request that this snapshot belongs to
parameters.name: approvalRequestId

parameters.description: Identifier of the specific snapshot to retrieve
parameters.name: snapshotId

operations.description:
Reorder product images to change their display sequence on the product detail page.

This operation allows sellers to adjust the display_order values of images associated with their product, which determines the visual sequence customers see when browsing the product. The first image in the reordered sequence becomes the main thumbnail image shown in search results and category listings.

Sellers can only reorder images for products they own. The operation requires the seller's authentication token and verifies ownership before applying any changes. All images for the product must be included in the reorder request to ensure a complete and consistent order sequence.

When images are reordered, the changes take effect immediately and are reflected in all customer-facing views without requiring product republishing. Each successful reorder operation is recorded in the product snapshot table for audit trail purposes.
operations.name: patchByProductid
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the requesting seller owns the product by checking product.seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID
2. Verify all image IDs in the reorder array belong to the specified product
3. Ensure all images for the product are included in the request (no images should be missing)
4. Validate that display_order values are unique integers starting from 0 (or 1, depending on schema convention)
5. Update the display_order field for each image record in the ecommerce_mall_product_images table
6. Create a product snapshot record to preserve the state before the reorder operation for audit trail
7. Update the search index to reflect any changes to the main thumbnail image (if the first image changed)
8. Return the complete updated list of product images sorted by the new display_order values
9. Handle edge case: if the main image was moved, update the product's cached main image reference
10. Return HTTP 200 with updated image list on success, HTTP 403 if seller doesn't own the product, HTTP 400 if validation fails

responseBody.description: Updated list of product images with new display order values

parameters.description: The UUID identifier of the product whose images are being reordered
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Array of image objects containing the image ID and its new display order value

operations.description:
Retrieve a hierarchical tree structure of all active product categories on the platform.

This operation returns a navigable category hierarchy that customers use to browse and discover products. The response organizes categories into a tree structure where each category may contain its child subcategories, respecting the one-level nesting limit defined in the system.

Categories are filtered to include only those with is_active=true, and are sorted by their display_order attribute within each parent level. Root categories (those without a parent) appear at the top level, with their subcategories nested beneath them.

The hierarchical structure enables intuitive customer navigation through the product catalog, allowing users to expand parent categories to view available subcategories and browse products by category.

Related operations:
- GET /categories - Lists all categories in flat format
- PATCH /categories - Browse categories with search and filter criteria
operations.name: tree
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_categories table for all categories where is_active = true and deleted_at is null.

Join the table with itself on parent_id to establish parent-child relationships. Each category's parent_id references another category's id, creating a hierarchical relationship.

Apply ordering by display_order ASC within each parent level to respect the catalog organization.

Transform the flat database result into a tree structure by grouping child categories under their respective parent categories. Root categories have null parent_id.

Validate that subcategories do not exceed one level of nesting by checking that subcategories themselves have no children.

Return the hierarchical tree structure with nested children arrays for each category level.

responseBody.description: Hierarchical tree structure of active categories with nested subcategories

operations.description:
Retrieve historical snapshots of an order item, including product, variant, and seller profile data as they existed at the time of purchase.

This operation provides access to immutable point-in-time records that preserve the exact state of the order item when it was created. These snapshots are essential for order verification, dispute resolution, and historical reference, ensuring that customers and administrators can review what was purchased even if the underlying products have been deleted or modified by the seller.

The response includes three types of snapshots: the product snapshot capturing product name, description, and pricing at purchase time; the variant snapshot preserving variant options and prices; and the seller profile snapshot showing the shop name and logo as they appeared when the order was placed. These snapshots remain accessible even after products are deleted or sellers close their accounts.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to order customers (who can view their own order items) and administrators (who have platform-wide visibility for oversight and dispute resolution purposes). All snapshot access is logged for accountability and audit trail purposes.
operations.name: snapshots
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_order_item_snapshots table for all snapshot records associated with the specified order item (itemId) within the given order (orderId).

Validate that the caller has appropriate access: the order customer who owns the order, or an administrator with platform-wide access. Use the order customer relationship from ecommerce_mall_orders.customer_id to verify ownership.

Join with product snapshot, variant snapshot, and seller profile snapshot data to return complete historical records. Include snapshot metadata such as created_at timestamp, actor reference (customer_id), and action type.

Apply access control based on entity ownership and administrative privileges. Customers can only access snapshots of order items from their own orders. Administrators can access snapshots across all orders.

Return the snapshots ordered by created_at in ascending order to show the chronological evolution of the order item's state. Include pagination if the number of snapshots exceeds a reasonable threshold (e.g., 100 records).

Ensure all snapshot data includes the preserved product name, variant options, prices, and seller shop information for accurate historical reference. Do not include any data that could be modified or deleted by sellers or customers.

responseBody.description: Collection of historical snapshots for the order item including product, variant, and seller profile data

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the order containing the item
parameters.name: orderId

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the order item within the order
parameters.name: itemId

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated review statistics for a specific product with filtering options.

This operation calculates and returns comprehensive statistics about all active reviews for the specified product, including the average rating, total review count, rating distribution across 1-5 stars, and verified purchase metrics.

**Data Source**:

Retrieves reviews from the ecommerce_mall_reviews table, filtering by the specified product ID and excluding soft-deleted reviews (where deleted_at is null). The endpoint supports multiple filter parameters to narrow down which reviews contribute to the statistics.

**Statistics Calculated**:

- Average rating across all matching reviews (weighted mean of 1-5 star ratings)
- Total review count from all matching reviews
- Rating distribution showing how many reviews received each star rating (1-star through 5-star)
- Verified purchase count (reviews where is_verified_purchase is true)
- Unverified purchase count (reviews from non-verified purchases)
- Most recent review date and oldest review date in the set

**Filtering Options**:

The operation supports optional filtering by verified purchase status, rating range, review date range, and other criteria. If no filters are specified, all active reviews for the product are included in the statistics.
operations.name: getReviewStats
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_reviews table for reviews matching the specified product_id with active status (deleted_at IS NULL).

Apply filters from the request body:
- is_verified_purchase: filter to only verified or only unverified reviews
- rating_min, rating_max: filter reviews by rating range (1-5)
- created_at_after, created_at_before: filter reviews by creation date range

Calculate aggregation statistics:
- AVG(rating) for average rating
- COUNT(*) for total count
- GROUP BY rating with COUNT for distribution
- MIN(created_at), MAX(created_at) for date range

Handle edge cases:
- Return null/empty stats if no matching reviews exist
- Calculate average with NULL-safe arithmetic to avoid division by zero
- Ensure rating distribution always includes all 5 rating levels even if count is 0

Return response body containing IEcommerceMallProductReviewStatsSummary.

responseBody.description: Aggregated review statistics for the specified product.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the product for which to retrieve review statistics.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Optional filter parameters to narrow which reviews contribute to the statistics.

operations.description:
Search and filter customer reviews for specific products or retrieve your review history.

This operation provides review retrieval capabilities with filtering based on product, rating, verification status, and text content. Customers can search reviews for products they are viewing, or filter their own review history using appropriate credentials.

The operation filters out deleted reviews automatically, ensuring only active reviews are returned. This aligns with the business rule that deleted reviews should not contribute to average rating calculations or be displayed on product pages.

Supports text search using trigram indexing on the review body for flexible content matching. Supports sorting by creation date (newest first by default) or by rating.

Pagination is required for efficient handling of large review datasets. The operation returns paginated results with cursor-based navigation for consistent pagination across multiple requests.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_reviews table with the following logic:

1. Build WHERE clause:
   - Filter by customer_id if provided in request body
   - Filter by product_id if provided in request body
   - Filter by is_verified_purchase if provided in request body
   - Filter by rating range (rating >= min, rating <= max) if provided
   - Filter by text search using body gin_trgm_ops index if search term provided
   - Always filter: deleted_at IS NULL to exclude deleted reviews

2. JOIN requirements:
   - Join with ecommerce_mall_customers to get customer display name (if customer_id not used as filter)
   - Handle deleted customer accounts: display 'deleted user' if customer was deleted

3. Sorting:
   - Default: created_at DESC (newest first)
   - Alternative: rating DESC, rating ASC

4. Pagination:
   - Apply page number and page size from request body
   - Return cursor-based pagination metadata

5. Response aggregation:
   - Return review summary with customer display name (or 'deleted user')
   - Include rating stars, title, body excerpt
   - Include created_at timestamp

6. Validation:
   - Validate rating filter values are integers between 1-5
   - Validate page and pageSize are positive integers
   - Validate search term length (min 2 chars, max 200 chars)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summaries with filtering and sorting metadata

requestBody.description: Search criteria including filters, pagination, and sorting options

operations.description:
Allows customers to vote on whether a product review is helpful or not helpful.

This operation enables the community-driven quality assessment system where customers can indicate whether they found a review helpful in their purchasing decision. Each vote contributes to the review's helpfulness score used for sorting reviews by relevance.

The operation supports both creating new votes and updating existing votes from the same customer on the same review. A customer can only have one vote per review, enforced by database constraints. When a customer changes their vote, the previous vote is updated rather than creating a duplicate.

Security and authorization:
- Only authenticated customers can cast helpfulness votes
- Guests cannot vote on review helpfulness
- Customers can only vote on reviews from products they have purchased (verified purchase requirement)
- Each customer can vote only once per review

Related operations:
- GET /products/{productId}/reviews - View product reviews where helpfulness votes influence sorting
- GET /customers/me/reviews - View reviews written by the current customer
operations.name: castHelpfulness
operations.specification:
Implement the helpfulness voting operation with the following logic:

1. Authentication validation:
   - Verify customer is authenticated (not guest)
   - Extract customer_id from authenticated session

2. Request body validation:
   - Validate review_id is provided and is a valid UUID
   - Validate helpfulness is a boolean (true or false)
   - Verify the review exists in ecommerce_mall_reviews
   - Verify the review is from a product the customer has purchased (check ecommerce_mall_orders and ecommerce_mall_order_items)

3. Vote upsert logic:
   - Check if a vote already exists for this customer_id + review_id combination
   - If exists: UPDATE the helpfulness value
   - If not exists: INSERT new vote record with current timestamp

4. Database operation:
   - Query ecommerce_mall_review_helpfulness_votes table
   - Check for existing vote using composite unique constraint
   - Perform upsert operation within transaction
   - Update created_at if new, updated_at always

5. Response:
   - Return the full vote record including id, customer_id, review_id, helpfulness, created_at, updated_at
   - If vote was deleted (soft delete), handle accordingly (allow re-vote or reject based on business rule)

6. Error handling:
   - 401 Unauthorized if not authenticated
   - 404 Not Found if review does not exist
   - 403 Forbidden if customer has not purchased the product
   - 400 Bad Request if helpfulness value is invalid

7. Business rules:
   - Respect soft delete on helpfulness votes (allow re-voting on deleted votes)
   - Ensure unique constraint on (customer_id, review_id) is not violated

responseBody.description: The helpfulness vote record that was created or updated

requestBody.description: Helpfulness vote details including the review to vote on and the vote value

operations.description:
Retrieve notification dashboard information for the authenticated actor.

This operation provides a comprehensive overview of notification status including unread count, recent notifications list, and system-wide alert status. The dashboard aggregates notification data from the ecommerce_mall_notifications table along with notification recipient tracking from ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients.

The response includes summary statistics such as total unread notifications, notification categories breakdown, and the 10 most recent notifications with their read status. Actors can quickly assess their notification state without querying individual notification records.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_notifications table filtered by the authenticated actor's notification reference table (ecommerce_mall_notification_of_customers, ecommerce_mall_notification_of_sellers, or ecommerce_mall_notification_of_admins).

Join with ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients to track read/unread status.

Calculate summary statistics: count of unread notifications, count by notification type/category, and retrieve the 10 most recent notifications ordered by createdAt descending.

Actor identification comes from the authentication context - customer, seller, admin, or super-admin sessions are identified via their respective session tables (ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions, ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions, ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions, ecommerce_mall_super_admin_sessions).

Only return notification data relevant to the authenticated actor's role and permissions. Admin actors may receive platform-wide notifications while customer and seller actors receive role-specific notifications.

responseBody.description: Notification dashboard summary information

operations.description:
Deliver a notification to specified actor(s) in the system.

This operation creates a new notification with title, body content, and type/category, then distributes it to one or more actor recipients. Notifications are system-initiated messages used for order status updates, seller approval notifications, platform announcements, and other platform events.

The notification system supports multiple actor types including customers, sellers, administrators, and super administrators. Each actor can receive notifications based on their role and relevant platform events.

When a notification is delivered, the system creates the notification record and establishes delivery relationships for each recipient actor through the polymorphic notification reference tables.
operations.name: deliver
operations.specification:
Create a notification record with provided title, body, and type.

1. Validate notification content: title (required, non-empty string), body (required, non-empty string), type (required, valid category from schema: 'order_update', 'seller_approval', 'platform_announcement', 'system_alert')

2. Validate recipients array: each recipient must have recipient_type ('customer', 'seller', 'admin', 'superAdmin', 'guest') and recipient_id (valid UUID referencing the appropriate actor table)

3. Create notification record with status='unread', created_at=now()

4. For each recipient:
   - Create ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients record with notification_id, recipient_type, recipient_id, read_status='unread'
   - If recipient_type='customer', create ecommerce_mall_notification_of_customers record
   - If recipient_type='seller', create ecommerce_mall_notification_of_sellers record
   - If recipient_type='admin', create ecommerce_mall_notification_of_admins record
   - If recipient_type='superAdmin', create ecommerce_mall_notification_of_super_admins record
   - If recipient_type='guest', create ecommerce_mall_notification_of_guests record

5. Return the created notification with full delivery confirmation details including all recipient records.

responseBody.description: Created notification with delivery confirmation

requestBody.description: Notification content and recipient information

type.description: Notification type/category for filtering and routing

recipient_type.description: Type of actor receiving the notification

recipients.description: List of actors to receive this notification

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistics of system-wide activity logs with comprehensive filtering capabilities.

This endpoint provides statistical summaries of platform activities across all actors (customers, sellers, administrators, super administrators). The aggregation returns grouped counts and metrics that enable administrators to monitor platform activity patterns, identify anomalies, and support dispute resolution investigations.

The aggregation supports multiple filter dimensions including time ranges, actor types, entity types, and action types. Results are returned as paginated aggregated data with summary statistics for each group.

Administrators can view aggregated activities to understand platform usage trends, detect suspicious activity patterns, and generate compliance reports. This operation is primarily used for oversight and audit purposes rather than day-to-day operational tasks.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_activity_logs table with aggregation grouping.

Apply filters on:
- Date range (created_at from/to)
- Actor types (customer, seller, admin, super_admin)
- Entity types (order, product, review, shipment, etc.)
- Action types (created, updated, deleted, approved, rejected, etc.)
- Soft delete exclusion (only active records where deleted_at is null)

Group activities by specified dimensions (e.g., by actor_type, by entity_type, by action_type, or by date).

Calculate aggregations:
- Count of activities per group
- Date range of activities per group
- Activity trends over time

Apply pagination with cursor-based navigation for large result sets.

Sort by aggregation count (descending) or by group key.

Return aggregated summary data with total count and pagination metadata.

responseBody.description: Paginated aggregated activity statistics

requestBody.description: Aggregation query parameters with filters, grouping, and pagination

operations.description:
Check the health status of the product search service.

This endpoint provides health information about the search index service used for product search functionality. It verifies that the search index table (ecommerce_mall_search_indices) is accessible and the search service is operational.

The health check returns the current status of the search service, timestamp of the last index update, and optional metrics about the search index health. This endpoint is designed for monitoring systems, load balancers, and external dependents to verify the search functionality is available before attempting product search operations.

No authentication is required for this health check endpoint as it provides only service availability information without exposing any sensitive data.
operations.name: check
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_search_indices table to verify database connectivity and retrieve index health metrics.

Implementation steps:
1. Establish connection to the search index database table
2. Perform a lightweight query to verify table accessibility (COUNT(*) or SELECT 1 LIMIT 1)
3. Retrieve the most recent index update timestamp from the table
4. Calculate the age of the last index update
5. Determine service status: healthy if index exists and was updated recently (e.g., within last hour), degraded if index is stale, unhealthy if table is inaccessible
6. Return health status with timestamp and any relevant metrics

Return 200 OK with health status object. Always return 200 even if status indicates degraded or unhealthy state - this allows monitoring systems to parse the status without HTTP error codes.

No authentication middleware required for this endpoint as it exposes only service availability information.

responseBody.description: Health status information for the search service

operations.description:
Trigger a reindexing job for search index entries across one or more entity types.

This operation initiates a background reindexing process that updates the search indices table with the latest data from Products, Categories, Reviews, and other indexed domains. The reindexing operation ensures search results reflect current product availability, pricing, and content.

Administrators and authorized system processes can request reindexing for specific entity types or trigger a full platform-wide reindex. The operation returns a job identifier that can be used to track reindexing progress.

The reindexing process runs asynchronously and does not block the API response. Once initiated, the system creates index entries with 'pending' status, processes the indexing in the background, and updates entries to 'active' status when complete.

This operation is commonly used after bulk product updates, when search results appear stale, or as part of scheduled maintenance tasks.
operations.name: reindex
operations.specification:
1. Accept request body with optional entityTypes array (['product', 'category', 'review', 'all'])
2. If entityTypes contains 'all', schedule reindexing for all entity types
3. If entityTypes contains specific types, schedule reindexing only for those types
4. Optionally accept entityIds array to reindex specific entity instances
5. Create a reindex job record in the job queue system with status 'queued'
6. Assign a unique job UUID for tracking
7. Return job details immediately without waiting for completion
8. Background worker picks up job and processes indexing
9. Update index entries to 'pending' status during processing
10. Update index entries to 'active' status when indexing completes successfully
11. If indexing fails for any entity, mark that entry with 'error' status
12. Return job status, entity count, and estimated completion time

responseBody.description: Details of the initiated reindexing job including job ID, target entity types, and status

requestBody.description: Parameters for the reindexing operation

operations.description:
Compare platform configuration values across different deployment environments.

This operation retrieves configuration definitions from the platform configurations table and fetches their values for specified environments, enabling administrators to identify configuration differences between staging, production, and other deployment scopes.

The endpoint supports filtering by configuration key patterns, environment scope selections, and active/inactive configuration status. Results are returned in a structured format showing each configuration's key, type, description, and value for each selected environment side-by-side for easy comparison.

Only configurations that exist in at least one of the selected environments are included in the results. Empty environments (no values for a configuration) are marked explicitly to distinguish between 'not configured' and 'no value provided'.
operations.name: compareEnvironments
operations.specification:
1. Parse request body to extract comparison criteria:
   - environmentScopes: Array of environment scope identifiers to compare (e.g., ['staging', 'production'])
   - configurationKeys: Optional array of configuration keys to filter by, or null for all
   - isActive: Optional boolean to filter active/inactive configurations only

2. Query ecommerce_mall_platform_configurations table with filters:
   - Apply isActive filter if provided
   - Apply configurationKeys filter if provided (using IN clause)
   - Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL)

3. For each configuration, fetch related values from ecommerce_mall_platform_configuration_values:
   - Join on configuration_id = ecommerce_mall_platform_configuration_id
   - Filter by environment_scopes IN (...) if provided
   - Include key, value, environment_scope columns

4. Transform results into comparison structure:
   - Group by configuration id
   - Create environment value map keyed by environment_scope
   - Mark missing environments as null value with undefined

5. Return paginated list with metadata:
   - Total count of configurations found
   - Current page and page size
   - Sort order applied

responseBody.description: Comparison result showing configuration values across selected environments (paginated)

requestBody.description: Comparison criteria including environments to compare and optional filters

operations.description:
Set a customer's shipping address as their default address for faster checkout.

This operation allows authenticated customers to designate one of their saved shipping addresses as their default. The default address is automatically pre-selected during checkout and simplifies the order placement process.

When an address is set as default, the system automatically unsets any previously designated default address for the same customer. This ensures only one default address exists per customer at any time, as enforced by the database's unique constraint on the (customer, is_default) combination in the ecommerce_mall_addresses table.

The operation verifies that the address belongs to the authenticated customer before making the update. Attempts to set another customer's address as default will be rejected with an unauthorized error.

The updated address is returned with the new is_default status and all other address fields unchanged. The address remains active and continues to be usable for order placement.

**Note**: This operation does not require a request body. The action is performed directly on the address specified in the path parameter.
operations.name: setDefault
operations.specification:
1. Extract addressId from path parameters and validate as UUID format.
2. Authenticate customer via JWT session token.
3. Query ecommerce_mall_addresses for address matching addressId AND ecommerce_mall_customer_id equals authenticated customer ID.
4. If address not found or does not belong to customer, return 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden.
5. If address.deleted_at is not null, return 400 Bad Request (cannot set deleted address as default).
6. Update address is_default to true.
7. Query all addresses for this customer where is_default=true AND id != addressId.
8. Update all those addresses to is_default=false (cascade unset previous default).
9. Save changes with updated_at timestamp.
10. Return updated address object with new is_default=true.

responseBody.description: Updated shipping address with is_default status set to true.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the shipping address to set as default.
parameters.name: addressId

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated cancellation request statistics for a seller's order items with optional filtering and grouping options.

This endpoint provides summary metrics about cancellation requests submitted by customers for order items associated with the seller's products. The statistics include counts grouped by cancellation status (pending, approved, rejected) and may include time-based breakdowns such as daily, weekly, or monthly trends.

The endpoint is primarily used by sellers to monitor their cancellation request workload, understand customer cancellation patterns, and track approval/rejection rates. The data helps sellers identify trends in customer behavior and optimize their cancellation approval policies.

Statistics are calculated based on the ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests table, filtering by the seller_id to show only requests relevant to the requesting seller's order items.

The request body supports filtering by date range (start_date, end_date) and grouping dimension (status, daily, weekly, monthly) to provide flexible analysis capabilities.
operations.name: getStatistics
operations.specification:
Query cancellation requests for the authenticated seller's order items.

Aggregate statistics by:
1. Total count of all cancellation requests
2. Count by status: pending, approved, rejected
3. Optional time-based breakdown (daily/weekly/monthly) if requested via grouping dimension
4. Average approval rate (approved / total non-pending)
5. Average processing time from request creation to approval/rejection

Apply seller context from authenticated user session - only include cancellation requests where seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID.

Filter by date range when start_date and end_date are provided in the request body to analyze statistics for specific time periods.

Group results by the specified dimension (status by default, or daily/weekly/monthly based on request). When grouping is applied, return both summary totals and detailed breakdown array.

Return aggregated statistics object with computed metrics. All numeric values should be integers or floats with appropriate precision.

Handle empty result sets by returning zero counts rather than 404. Statistics are real-time calculations, not cached.

responseBody.description: Aggregated cancellation request statistics for the seller's order items

requestBody.description: Filter and grouping options for the statistics query

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistics and analytics about refund requests across the platform.

This operation provides a comprehensive overview of refund request metrics including total counts, status breakdowns, approval rates, and trend data. The data is aggregated from the ecommerce_mall_refund_requests table and can be used for dashboard displays, administrative monitoring, and business intelligence purposes.

The analytics include:
- Total number of refund requests in the system
- Breakdown by status (pending, approved, rejected, refunded)
- Approval and rejection rates as percentages
- Recent activity statistics (last 30 days, last 7 days)
- Average processing time for resolved requests
- Seller-level refund statistics (for seller accounts viewing their shop analytics)

This operation is typically used by administrators and sellers to monitor platform health and understand refund patterns. The data is computed on-the-fly from the current state of refund request records.
operations.name: getAnalytics
operations.specification:
Query aggregated statistics from ecommerce_mall_refund_requests table.

1. Calculate total count of all refund requests
2. Group and count requests by status field (pending, approved, rejected, refunded)
3. Calculate approval rate: (approved + refunded) / total * 100
4. Calculate rejection rate: rejected / total * 100
5. For seller context: filter statistics to only include order items owned by the authenticated seller
6. Calculate average time from submitted_at to decision_at for resolved requests (approved/rejected)
7. Count requests created in last 7 days and last 30 days
8. Return all metrics in a single response object

Handle edge cases:
- Return zero values when no refund requests exist
- Handle null decision_at times when calculating average processing time
- Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at is null)
- If seller context exists, join with ecommerce_mall_order_items to filter by seller_snapshot_id

responseBody.description: Aggregated analytics and statistics about refund requests

operations.description:
Approve or reject a customer's refund request for an order item.

This endpoint allows the seller to respond to a refund request submitted by a customer. The seller must be the seller who sold the specific order item referenced in the refund request. Only sellers can respond to refund requests for their products; customers cannot approve or reject their own refund requests.

The seller provides an approval decision (approve or reject) along with an optional comment explaining the decision. When the seller responds, a snapshot of the refund request state is created to maintain an audit trail of the seller's action and the request state at the time of response.

If the seller approves the refund request:
- The refund request status changes to 'approved'
- The order item status changes to 'refunded'
- Stock quantity is restored via an inventory record update
- If all items in the order are refunded, the order status becomes 'refunded'
- The customer receives the refund for that specific item

If the seller rejects the refund request:
- The refund request status changes to 'rejected'
- The order item remains in 'delivered' status
- No refund is processed
- The item stock is not affected

Before responding, the seller should verify that the refund request meets validation criteria: the order item status must be 'delivered', the request must be within seven days of the delivery date, and the request must not have been previously responded to.

Related operations: PATCH /refund-requests/{refundRequestId} to view refund request details, PATCH /refund-requests to list refund requests.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification: Retrieve the refund request by refundRequestId from ecommerce_mall_refund_requests table. Verify the requesting seller is the seller of the order item by joining with order_items and products tables. Validate that the refund request is in pending approval state. Validate that the request is within seven days of delivery date. If action is 'approve': create refund request snapshot with seller action recorded, update order item status to 'refunded', update refund request status to 'approved', process refund by creating inventory record to restore stock quantity, check if all order items are refunded and update order status to 'refunded' if applicable. If action is 'reject': create refund request snapshot with seller action recorded, update refund request status to 'rejected'. Return the updated refund request with new state. Handle validation errors: refund request not found, seller not authorized (not the seller of the item), refund request not in pending state, refund request expired (beyond 7 days from delivery), refund request already responded to.

responseBody.description: Updated refund request with new state after seller response

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the refund request to be approved or rejected
parameters.name: refundRequestId

requestBody.description: Approval or rejection decision for the refund request

prerequisites.description: Customer must create a refund request for an order item before a seller can approve or reject it. The approval operation transitions an existing refund request from pending to approved/rejected state.

operations.description:
Reject a customer's refund request for a delivered order item.

This operation allows the seller who sold the item to reject a pending refund request submitted by the customer. When rejecting, the seller must provide a detailed rejection reason explaining why the refund was denied. This reason is recorded in the refund request and visible to the customer.

Upon successful rejection, the refund request status changes from 'pending' to 'rejected'. A snapshot of the rejection action is created, recording who rejected (seller identity), when the rejection occurred, the rejection reason provided, and the state of the refund request at the time of rejection. The snapshot serves as an immutable audit record for dispute resolution and compliance purposes.

The rejection is final—rejected refund requests cannot be resubmitted by the customer. The customer can view the rejection reason and may choose to escalate the matter to platform support or contact the seller directly for resolution. The order item remains in 'delivered' status and no refund is processed.

Only the seller who owns the order item associated with the refund request can perform this operation. Other actors including the customer who submitted the request, other sellers, and platform administrators (without escalation privileges) cannot reject the request through this endpoint.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the refund request exists and is owned by the calling seller's order item
2. Verify the refund request status is 'pending' - reject only pending requests
3. Validate the 7-day delivery window: check that delivery_date + 7 days has not elapsed (customer eligibility already validated at creation, but re-validate for consistency)
4. Validate that the seller is authenticated and has permission to reject this specific refund request (verify seller_id matches the order item's seller)
5. Validate rejection_reason is provided and meets minimum length requirements (typically 10-500 characters)
6. Begin database transaction
7. Update ecommerce_mall_refund_requests table:
   - Set status to 'rejected'
   - Set seller_response to the rejection reason provided
   - Set rejection_reason to the rejection reason (or null if not explicitly tracked)
   - Set decision_at to current timestamp
8. Create snapshot in ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots table:
   - Set refund_request_id to the refund request ID
   - Set actor_type to 'seller'
   - Set action_type to 'rejected'
   - Set status_before to 'pending'
   - Set status_after to 'rejected'
   - Set response_before to null (no prior response)
   - Set response_after to rejection_reason
   - Set created_at to current timestamp
9. Create snapshot subtype record in ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshot_of_sellers table referencing this snapshot
10. Commit transaction
11. Return updated refund request with rejection details

Error handling:
- 404 if refund request does not exist
- 403 if caller is not the seller who owns the order item
- 409 if refund request is not in 'pending' status (already approved/rejected)
- 400 if rejection_reason is missing or too short
- 500 if database transaction fails

responseBody.description: The updated refund request with rejection details recorded

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the refund request to reject
parameters.name: refundRequestId

requestBody.description: Rejection details including the reason for denying the refund request

operations.description:
Retrieve a list of pending refund requests awaiting seller response for the authenticated seller's products.

This operation returns all refund requests with 'pending' status that were submitted by customers for order items containing the seller's products. Each refund request includes the customer's refund reason, evidence description, delivery date, and the refund request code for reference.

The refund request status 'pending' indicates the seller has not yet approved or rejected the refund request. Sellers must review each request and take action through the approve or reject operations. The seller can view customer-provided reasons and any evidence descriptions to make informed decisions.

This endpoint is restricted to seller actors only. Customers cannot view pending refund requests through this endpoint - they should use their own refund request listing to see the status of their submissions.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_refund_requests table where status='pending' and the refund request's order item belongs to a product owned by the authenticated seller.

Join with:
- ecommerce_mall_refund_requests.customer for customer name and email
- ecommerce_mall_refund_requests.ecommerce_mall_order_item_id -> ecommerce_mall_order_items.product_snapshot_id -> ecommerce_mall_products.seller_id

Filter conditions:
- refund_requests.status = 'pending'
- order_items.seller_snapshot_id = seller's id (or match via product snapshot to seller)
- refund_requests.deleted_at IS NULL (exclude soft-deleted requests)

Apply search filters from requestBody on customer name, email, refund reason, delivery date range, and submitted date range.

Order results by submitted_at descending (most recent first), then by created_at descending.

Return paginated list with:
- Page number and size from requestBody
- Total count for pagination metadata
- Array of refund request summaries

Authorization: Seller actor only. The seller_id from JWT token determines which seller's products are included in results.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of pending refund request summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for pending refund requests

operations.description:
Retrieve the current operational status and health information of the ecommerce mall platform.

This endpoint provides a comprehensive overview of platform availability and key business metrics. It returns the current status of all business categories including order statuses (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially completed) and shipment statuses (created, in transit, delivered) as defined in the business rules.

The status information is useful for monitoring platform health, troubleshooting issues, and providing external services with real-time platform state information. All status values are derived from the actual database state and reflect the current operational condition of the system.
operations.name: status
operations.specification: Query system health indicators and business status aggregates. Return platform availability status, active order counts by status, active shipment counts by status, and overall system health score. This endpoint should be lightweight and fast to respond as it may be called frequently by monitoring systems and health check probes.

responseBody.description: Platform status and health information

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.

session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.

IEcommerceMallInventoryRecord.description: Complete inventory record entity representing a single stock movement event in the product variant's audit trail. Tracks quantity changes (positive for incoming stock such as restocks and returns, negative for outgoing stock such as sales and cancellations), reason categorization for the movement type, and transaction classification. Includes optional references to the orders, cancellation requests, or refund requests that triggered the stock movement. Immutable business data (quantity_change, reason, type, remaining_quantity) that cannot be modified once created, ensuring a complete and accurate history of all stock movements.
IEcommerceMallInventoryRecord.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_inventory_records table. Relations joined from ecommerce_mall_product_variants (variant), ecommerce_mall_orders (order), ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests (cancellationRequest), ecommerce_mall_refund_requests (refundRequest). Quantity_change is Int (positive for incoming stock like restocks/returns, negative for outgoing like sales/cancellations). Remaining_quantity preserves stock level after each movement. Reason categorizes movement type (RESTOCK, SALE, RETURN, CANCELLATION, ADJUSTMENT, DAMAGE, LOSS, etc.). Type classifies transaction (INCOMING, OUTGOING, ADJUSTMENT). Soft delete supported via deleted_at for data preservation.

IEcommerceMallInventoryRecord.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering and browsing inventory movement records.

This request body accepts optional filters to narrow down inventory records by variant, stock movement reason, transaction type, date range, quantity change amount, or full-text search. Pagination parameters control how many records are returned per page and which page to retrieve.

Filter parameters are all optional, allowing flexible searching. When no filters are provided, the API returns the first page of all inventory records for the authenticated user's products. The search field performs full-text search across reason and description fields using trigram indexing for efficient fuzzy matching.
IEcommerceMallInventoryRecord.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query parameter filters for inventory records:

1. variantId: Filter by specific product variant (UUID)
2. reason: Filter by stock movement reason (RESTOCK, SALE, RETURN, CANCELLATION, ADJUSTMENT, etc.)
3. type: Filter by transaction type (INCOMING, OUTGOING, ADJUSTMENT)
4. dateRange: Filter created_at within range (from/to date-time)
5. quantityChangeRange: Filter quantity_change amount (min/max integers)
6. search: Full-text search on reason/description fields (uses trigram index)
7. page: Page number (1-indexed, minimum 1)
8. limit: Page size (1-100, minimum 1)
9. sortBy: Sort field (created_at, quantity_change, reason)
10. sortDirection: Sort order (ASC, DESC)

All fields optional - empty request returns all records with default pagination.
Pagination defaults: page=1, limit=20.
Sorting defaults: sortBy=created_at, sortDirection=DESC.

IEcommerceMallReview.ICreate.x-autobe-specification:
Create a new product review record in ecommerce_mall_reviews table.

1. Validate customer authentication - reject if unauthenticated (customer identity from JWT session)
2. Verify order item status is 'delivered' before allowing review creation (check related order in ecommerce_mall_orders)
3. Validate uniqueness constraint - reject if customer already has a review for this product in this order (unique constraint: customer_id + product_id + order_id)
4. Validate rating is an integer between 1 and 5
5. Validate body text is provided and not empty
6. Validate product_id references a valid product (exists in ecommerce_mall_products)
7. Validate order_id references a valid order (exists in ecommerce_mall_orders) and contains the specified product
8. Set is_verified_purchase to true (order provides proof of purchase)
9. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
10. Set deleted_at to null (active review)
11. Insert record into ecommerce_mall_reviews table
12. Return the created review object with all fields including generated id

Business rules: Customer must be authenticated. Each customer can write only one review per product per order. Order must have 'delivered' status. Rating range: 1-5 stars. Body required, title optional.

IEcommerceMallNotification.ICreate.x-autobe-specification:
Create a new notification record in ecommerce_mall_notifications table with the provided title, body, and type. Status is automatically set to 'unread' by the server.

Request body mapping:
- title: Mapped directly to ecommerce_mall_notifications.title. Required, max 255 characters.
- body: Mapped directly to ecommerce_mall_notifications.body. Required, non-empty string.
- type: Mapped directly to ecommerce_mall_notifications.type. Required, must be one of: order_update, seller_approval, platform_announcement, system_alert, cancellation_decision, refund_decision, shipment_update.
- recipients: Array of recipient objects that specifies which actors should receive this notification. Each recipient object contains actor_type and actor_id. The server creates notification_recipients junction records and actor-specific reference records (notification_of_customers, notification_of_sellers, notification_of_admins, notification_of_super_admins, or notification_of_guests) for each recipient.

Transaction behavior: All operations complete within a single database transaction. If any recipient validation fails (actor doesn't exist or actor_type mismatch), roll back all changes.

Actor reference creation:
- For customer recipients: Create ecommerce_mall_notification_of_customers record and ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients record with actor_type='customer'
- For seller recipients: Create ecommerce_mall_notification_of_sellers record and ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients record with actor_type='seller'
- For admin recipients: Create ecommerce_mall_notification_of_admins record and ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients record with actor_type='admin'
- For superAdmin recipients: Create ecommerce_mall_notification_of_super_admins record and ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients record with actor_type='superAdmin'
- For guest recipients: Create ecommerce_mall_notification_of_guests record and ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients record with actor_type='guest'

Validation rules:
- title: required, non-empty, max 255 characters
- body: required, non-empty string
- type: required, must match one of the 7 allowed enum values
- recipients: required, non-empty array with at least one recipient object
- Each recipient must have valid actor_type and actor_id that exists in the database

- product_id: Extracted from request body, must be valid UUID pointing to available product in ecommerce_mall_products
- customer_id: Resolved from authenticated customer JWT session, NOT in request body

- Status filtering: Filter by request status (pending, approved, rejected)
- Date range filtering: Filter by creation date range (from/to)

- Sorting: Sort results by different fields in ascending or descending order

Immutable snapshot record that captures the state of a refund request at a specific point in time during the refund workflow. Each snapshot serves as an audit trail entry documenting status transitions, reason changes, seller responses, and actor accountability for dispute resolution and compliance purposes.

Snapshots are created automatically when sellers respond to refund requests (approval or rejection) and preserve the complete before/after value comparisons. They provide an authoritative historical record of the entire refund request lifecycle from submission through resolution.

Authorized actors who can view snapshots include the customer who initiated the refund request, the seller who responded, and platform administrators (admin and superAdmin) for dispute resolution and auditing.

Access controlled by actor authorization: customer verifies refund request ownership via ecommerce_mall_refund_requests.ecommerce_mall_customer_id, seller verifies order item's product ownership via ecommerce_mall_refund_requests.ecommerce_mall_order_item_id + ecommerce_mall_products.seller_id, admin/super_admin always authorized.
